LESSON: TOILETING

Grade: PP1
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: MORAL 4.1 Islamic Etiquette By the end of the sub strand • Learners are shown pi
Topic 4.1.2: Toileting

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Toileting. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do we enter the learner should be able to: leaving the toilet according to Islamic and leave the toilet?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain what Toileting means in simple pupil language
2. give 3 correct examples of Toileting from Kenya
3. practise Toileting in clear steps
4. apply Toileting in one real-life situation this week

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: TOILETING
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: PP1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Toileting helps you succeed in ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: TOILETING
Study Toileting like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Explain what Toileting means in simple pupil language

What this means
In this part you learn to explain what Toileting means in simple pupil language. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain what Toileting means in simple pupil language.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Toileting” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain what Toileting means in simple pupil language. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Give 3 correct examples of Toileting from Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to give 3 correct examples of Toileting from Kenya. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: give 3 correct examples of Toileting from Kenya.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Toileting in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can give 3 correct examples of Toileting from Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Practise Toileting in clear steps

What this means
In this part you learn to practise Toileting in clear steps. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practise Toileting in clear steps.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practise Toileting in clear steps. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Apply Toileting in one real-life situation this week

What this means
In this part you learn to apply Toileting in one real-life situation this week. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply Toileting in one real-life situation this week.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Toileting” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply Toileting in one real-life situation this week. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Toileting is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Toileting” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: explain what Toileting means in simple pupil language)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Toileting in your own words. (skill: give 3 correct examples of Toileting from Kenya)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: practise Toileting in clear steps)

Example 4: Show how “Toileting” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: apply Toileting in one real-life situation this week)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Toileting to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain what Toileting means in simple pupil language.
3. Practise this skill: give 3 correct examples of Toileting from Kenya.
4. Practise this skill: practise Toileting in clear steps.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Toileting from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Toileting: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP1 learner study Toileting?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we enter the learner should be able to: leaving the toilet according to Islamic and leave the toilet?
2. How do we use the lessons) manners of entering and educational materials. toilet properly?
3. What do we do after b) identify proper way of the proper use of toilet. leaving the toilet?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Toileting means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain what Toileting means in simple pupil language.
5. Be able to: give 3 correct examples of Toileting from Kenya.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
